data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone X offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a dual speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone X users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones. The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

  • Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos.
  • Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording.
  • Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.
  • Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone X has at least 3 different microphones in different places for the phone for different purposes

  • The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls
  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

  • Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.
  • Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.
  • Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works
  • If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone X
  • Go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore, saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

  • ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error code – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

  • To check if your iPhone is updated
  • To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)
  • If the update still fails try updating from another pc.
  • Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.
  • Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.

If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.   • Network never reaches the full level.

  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.
  • To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

The new iPhone X offers one of the best displays consisting of a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone X have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone X is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display
  • iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone X comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode
  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all.

data.title: Rear Camera Replacement
data.description:
Apple revolutionized the entire line of iPhones with the iPhone X series. The iPhone X offers a triple camera setup of 3 different lenses with LED flash. Which easily makes iPhone X the best in its business. Even with such an amazing camera, it has been found that some users have found some issues regarding the camera. The most common issues regarding the rear camera of iPhone X found in the apple support forum and internet are:

  • Black Display when the camera turns on/ nothing shows in the camera
  • LED Flash is not working
  • Photos seem too noisy/ grainy
  • Camera or the iPhone freezes while zooming in
  • Camera freezes/ shows black screen after an iOS update
  • Blurry, unclear photos

Out of Sync flash. This is a problem where a user wants to take a photo with the flash, but the flash gets triggered after the photo has been taken.

These are the most common issues that are often reported by users in Apple service centers and user forums. However, they are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available that works as a remedy for these issues. If you are facing any of the above-mentioned problems, try doing

  • Removing any protective cases for your phone. Especially metallic or magnetic cases, which may hamper the proper functioning of your phone’s camera.
  • Try Restarting your phone.
  • Try Cleaning your lenses with a microfiber cloth. Be careful not to scratch it.
  • If your camera flash isn’t working, try turning on flash from the control center and see if it works.
  • Try disabling Voiceover settings for your iPhone. From Settings > General > Accessibility > Turn off voiceover
  • Try Switching between camera lenses in settings.
  • You can also try resetting previous settings.

If none of the solutions work for you, you might need to get your iPhone looked at by professionals. data.title: Wifi Issue
data.description:
However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone X. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone X Wi-Fi issues are…

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone X.
  • Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone X are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone X’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.
  • Restore the default network connection

( Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

data.title: Boot Loop
data.description:
Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that.

This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

  • Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)
  • Battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.
  • Hardware Damage.
  • Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.
  • If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.
  • Force Restart Your iPhone X

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo). Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly. Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone X is one of the best phones in the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancellation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio-only comes out of the right speaker grill and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone X are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone X users are:

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/Low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.
  • Phone stuck in Headphone mode
  • Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are:

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone X
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.
  • Try removing any protective cases
  • Clean the speaker grills for dirt and debris

data.title: Charging Dock Replacement
data.description:
The new iPhone X comes with a lightning port which is one of the most important parts of the smartphone. It can be charged with a lightning cable and charges at a whopping 18 Watt (fast charging). This can charge your phone to 50 percent in 30 minutes. And it can also be used as a USB 2.0 port. However, after using the phone for a long time or by an accident; your charging dock of the phone may get faulty or damaged, and you might need to get it replaced.

The most common issues of the iPhone X charging dock are:

  • The battery charges very slowly
  • iPhone X not charging beyond 80 %.
  • Charging Not available or Liquid has been detected in the charging port error.
  • The charging dock can’t be connected to a USB-supported device through the lightning cable.

If your phone has any one of these issues or something not mentioned in the list of the common issues. You will still like to check out these DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may solve the problem regarding the charging dock in your iPhone X.

  • Make sure you don’t have any debris or dirt on your charging dock. This may prevent charging.
  • Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty.
  • Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone X. if you do have it make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%.
  • Disable optimized Charging in here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health.

Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

  • If your phone is wet, wait until it is dry to charge your phone.

If none of the fixes cut it for you, you may need to get your phone looked at by professionals.
